<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert"></a>

## Station control and the Seifert service exchange

**Sources on this page:** p168 A, p168 B. [Concise case study](../radio/seifert.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p169 A](169.md#source-p169-a), [p172 A](172.md#source-p172-a), [p172 B](172.md#source-p172-b), [p174 B](174.md#source-p174-b), [p174 C](174.md#source-p174-c), [p174 D](174.md#source-p174-d), [p174 E](174.md#source-p174-e).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-station-control-and-the-seifert-service-exchange"></a>


[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All cases](../README.md) · [Source certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/seifert_records.json) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Nine source records, seven message groups.** The November 7–9 and November 10–12 published keys recover a sequence of radio-station reports and short service messages. Two pairs are repeated transmissions. These records are outside the original 22-entry challenge; the open p170 challenge is section **A**, not any of these neighboring records.

Source transcription, cipher checks and editorial work: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The station-control interpretations of p168 A and B were already published by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker**; their author manuscript discusses both on printed p. 23 / PDF p. 24. The keys retain their recorded historical and modern provenance. This page provides a source-level edition, without claiming a first historical decipherment.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-conditional-shared-digits"></a>

### Conditional shared digits

The paired monitoring orders each gain their hundreds digit: **500**. Both physical receptions have the same complete ciphertext; repetition preserves the value once the shared square is interpreted. No source coordinate is changed. The [joint reconstruction](../../experiments/nov10_joint_completion/README.md) combines the earlier Marineamt and formation interpretations with the army-number constraint and the mobilization decree; the reversed 7/9 assignment is retained there.

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the joint square:**

> Sofort US 500 hoeren.


<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-read-the-messages"></a>

### Read the messages

The prior body credit for p168 A also applies to its repeated content at
**p169 A**. Identification of the repeat, its exact coordinate differences,
and the present source edition remain our contribution.

Square brackets mark supplied letters or abbreviation expansions. Punctuation, capitalization and word spacing are editorial.

| Source | Readable German | Meaning and exact qualification |
|---|---|---|
| **p168 A**; repeated with errors at **p169 A** | Stehe ab 2200 unter Aufsicht Sol[d]atenrats. Stat[ion und] Personal fest in meiner Hand. Betrieb unverändert. Seifert. | From 22:00 the sender is under the soldiers' council's supervision; station/personnel remain firmly under his control and operation is unchanged. All 92 raw positions of p168 A decode exactly; the source spells `SOLATENRATS` without `D`. The connecting words in the `STATPERSONAL` expansion are editorial. |
| **p168 B** | Soldatenrat Cöln wird bald Funkstelle besetzen. Versucht schon Funksprüche aufzugeben. | Cologne's soldiers' council is expected to occupy the radio station and is already trying to submit radio messages. The raw text has `SOLDATENRA9` and `SCKON`; the readable version requires two explicit coordinate substitutions. |
| **p172 A** | Akten [s]ämtlich vernichtet. Schlüssel in pers[önlicher] Obhut noch vorhanden. Seifert. | All records have been destroyed; the cipher keys remain in personal custody. The source fixes 67/68 plaintext positions. One invalid printed glyph leaves the initial letter of `SAEMTLICH` unresolved; `S` is a supported reading, not a source-observed letter. |
| **p174 B** | Wenn Seifert eingetroffe[n], bitte Nachr[icht]. TOF. | Please report when Seifert has arrived. The source fixes 36/37 positions. One doubtful glyph permits `N`; a `G` interpretation of that glyph instead produces separator `X` after the raw spelling `EINGETROFFE`. `TOF` is not expanded. |
| **p174 C** | Wann Rückkunft Seifert? RE. | When will Seifert return? All 24 plaintext positions decode exactly. `RE` remains unexpanded. |
| **p172 B / p174 D** | Sofort US ?00 hören. | An immediate listening instruction. The two 40-coordinate copies are identical. The unknown hundreds digit can be **5, 6, 7, 8 or 9** under a globally consistent completion of the published square. The role of `US` and the units of the number are not established. |
| **p174 E** | Seifert abgefahren. RENTE. | Seifert has departed. The raw text is `SQIFQRTABGEFAHRENXRENTE`; restoring the name requires two explicit `G → X` coordinate substitutions. `RENTE` is retained literally. |

The shared surname connects the service records, but the surviving headers do not establish Seifert's full name or a complete itinerary. The printed time expressions are preserved in the certificate, including the anomalous `17.28 p.m.` in p174 E. The day digit in p172 B is overtyped; the identical p174 D copy is explicitly dated 12 November.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-evidence-and-reproduction"></a>

### Evidence and reproduction

The [certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/seifert_records.json) contains all nine literal source transcriptions, original headers, partial keys, raw plaintext domains, cropped-image hashes and exact proposed edits. It applies the already published keys; no unknown square cell is fixed by the prose.

```sh
python experiments/p170_continuation/verify_seifert.py
python experiments/p170_continuation/verify_seifert.py --json
```

The independent verifier checks **913 source slots**, every source-preserving fill, the four explicit coordinate substitutions, the p169 deletion aliases, both identical service copies, and all five globally attainable digit readings. A local copy of the source PDF can additionally be bound by SHA-256 with `--pdf /path/to/childs.pdf`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-seifert-sources-and-priority"></a>

#### Sources and priority

- **J. Rives Childs collection:** printed pp. 168, 169, 172 and 174; PDF pp. 171, 172, 175 and 177 in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view). The certificate retains its hash and the exact section headers.
- **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker:** *Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*, [author manuscript](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf), printed p. 23 / PDF p. 24. This earlier work explicitly identifies the p168 A/B station-control reports; it also credits Childs's wartime decipherment of the Cologne message. The present edition does not reassign that priority.
- **Published keys:** [key catalog](../../data/keys.json), entries `Nov7-9` and `Nov10-12`, retaining original table and solver provenance.

## p168 C — Full Munich routing witness for order 11338

**Sources on this page:** p168 C. [Concise case study](../radio/p168_munich_routing_witness.md).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p168-munich-routing-witness-p168-c--full-munich-routing-witness-for-order-11338"></a>



**Source-frame recovery and review: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 4 November 2026.**
The full p168 C retransmission now has a **139/140-position raw certificate**.
The irregular six-coordinate and four-coordinate groups require an explicit
frame repair: exclude one repeated D and add one unknown coordinate. A V
observed in the corresponding p159 B group supplies that gap, producing a
**140/140-position source-linked stream**. These fixed counts retain the
message's word garbles and numerical labels.

The p168 observation also reads **GEN KDO**, supporting one coordinate repair
of the p159 component's `GEN HDO`. This extends the [p158 component edition](#edition-cases-p158);
it is a full witness certificate for an existing record, not a newly found
message or a claim to first decipherment of order 11338.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p168-munich-routing-witness-source-and-frame"></a>

### Source and frame

Childs, printed p168 / PDF p171, section C:
`RVV v N4 (9.03 p.m., November 9th); 1803 VON SY ZU CHI 156 U 69; RICHI-280`.
The separate `1803` field is retained literally. The [original page crop](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p168_CD.png)
also shows the following section D.

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — all 280 observed coordinates, with irregular groups retained:**

```text
GDDFV DXFDD AVVFG XXVDD XVADD VVFGV VDDVV DVAXV
XVGVV GVXDD XVVVG VVVGV DDGDX VAVGG AAAXG AVFAD
VDADDD VAXVD VVDDD GADAX FAXXF GFFXF XDVVD DXDGD
DAXVA VDXVV XDVDV DXDGD XGVFV VGGVD FVVAV DFDAD
VDFXV XDAXG VXVVD DDAGX DVDGD DDGDX DXXXD VVVG
VGVXV VVVFA DDXVD XGXDX AVFDX VGVXV VVVVG VVXDV
VXADX VXDDV GXAVV GDVAA DGDVF VXFVX GFAXD DGDFA
```

</details>

Rows 3 and 5 contain 41 and 39 coordinates respectively. The six-coordinate
`VDADDD` is source[80:86]; the four-coordinate `VVVG` is source[196:200]. Their
length discrepancies cancel, so the literal body already has the advertised
280 coordinates. Treating both as regular five-coordinate groups without an
explicit operation would conceal the source error.

The primary frame excludes the D at source 83 and inserts one unknown at
boundary 195 of the remaining 279-slot stream, at the start of the short group.
All other 279 observations remain unchanged and in source order. This is a
conditional reconstruction, not an OCR correction. All indices here are zero
based; ranges are half open.

There are **12 tied descriptions**: exclude any of source 83,84,85 and insert
at any boundary 195,196,197,198. A source-directed comparison checks all 30
choices within the six-coordinate and four-coordinate groups. The twelve
leaders have six disagreements against the independently observed coordinates
of the p159 B component; coordinates already supplied from another copy are
excluded from that comparison. The comparison establishes correspondence,
not a unique historical error mechanism.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p168-munich-routing-witness-new-coordinate-support-for-kdo"></a>

### New coordinate support for KDO

At plaintext position 16, p168 C has the fully observed pair **VG = K**.
Its model indices 113 and 169 come from source 114 and 170. The corresponding
p159 B component has **VX = H**. Thus its `GEN HDO` can be repaired to `GEN KDO`
using the observed G from p168 source 170:

| Receiving source | Source index | Printed | Parallel-supported replacement |
|---|---:|:---:|:---:|
| p159 B | 169 | X | G |

This is one observed-coordinate substitution in p159 B, supported by a separate
printed observation. It changes exactly one plaintext letter and preserves all
other text in the established `p159B_supported_V` component layer.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — earlier p159 B supported-V component plus the single X→G substitution at source169; all other inherited repairs and garbles retained:**

```text
UEBER2XBAYRXGENXKDOXMUENCXENXXAN7XRSSXDIVXXLA3DSBERGXAN0LECHXXNICHTDURCHKABELXARMEESCHLUESSELDOWPELTXEMPFANGBESTXXOXHXLXRMX1ANRX11338GEHXORX
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p168-munich-routing-witness-joint-source-reconciliation"></a>

### Joint-source reconciliation

The last displayed stream also has an explicit reconciliation of the p168
witness. It follows the established p159 component at the remaining source
disagreements and uses the new p168 observation for KDO. Each selected
coordinate has a printed donor; these are recorded choices between differing
observations, not word guesses or an automatic majority vote.

| Reconciliation | p168 observed substitutions | p168 added-slot fills | p159 additional observed substitutions | Cable word |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| p159 B and p168 C | 5 | 1, V from p159 B | 1, G from p168 C | `1ABEL` retained |
| Add p158 D as third witness | 6 | 1, V from p159 B | 1, G from p168 C | `KABEL` |

The three-witness version is exactly the p159 B + KDO stream displayed above.
Its six substitutions in the primary p168 frame have the following donors:

| p168 source index | Printed | Selected | Original donor |
|---:|:---:|:---:|---|
| 5 | D | V | p159 B source 5 |
| 7 | F | V | p158 D source 7 |
| 169 | X | V | p159 B source 168 |
| 174 | V | D | p159 B source 173 |
| 175 | D | V | p159 B source 174 |
| 247 | D | X | p159 B source 247 |

At model 7, original p159 B has invalid `R`; its earlier V reconstruction must
not be counted as an independent p159 observation. The V here comes directly
from p158 D source 7, in its established prefix correspondence. The two-witness
layer therefore keeps p168's F at that position and retains `1ABEL`. Both layers
keep `DOWPELT` unchanged; no P is invented to make `DOPPELT`. The native sources,
primary raw reading and one-V source-linked layer above remain separate.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p168-munich-routing-witness-reproduction-and-credit"></a>

The [certificate](../../experiments/p168_munich_routing_witness/certificates.json)
records the literal source, every coordinate origin, all raw character domains,


<a id="edition-cases-p158"></a>

## p158 — Composite routing and key instructions

**Sources on this page:** p168 D. [Concise case study](../p158.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p158](158.md#source-p158), [p159 B](159.md#source-p159-b), [p159 C](159.md#source-p159-c).

<a id="edition-cases-p158-p158--composite-routing-and-key-instructions"></a>



The historical p158 D record combines portions of two routing instructions under the published **Nov7–9** key. We identified its prefix with p159 B and its suffix with p159 C; repeated transmissions on p168 C/D support the component readings and several source repairs.

<a id="edition-cases-p158-most-likely-component-readings"></a>

### Most likely component readings

**Component B, from the p159/p168 witnesses:**

**Readable German — excerpt of the component reconstruction; bracketed expansions remain editorial:**

> Ueber 2. bayr. Gen.-[Kdo.], [Muenchen], an 7. [unit unclear] Div., [Landsberg an/am Lech]. Nicht durch Kabel. Armeeschluessel [doppelt]. Empfang [bestaetigen]. O.H.L. […] 11338 geh. […]

**Component C, from the p159/p168 witnesses:**

**Readable German — excerpt of the component reconstruction; bracketed expansions remain editorial:**

> Ueber 2. bair. Gen.-Kmd., Muenchen, an 4. bair. Div., [Innsbruck]. Nicht durch [Kabel]. [Armee-CHI] doppelt. Empfang [bestaetigen]. An O.H.L. […]

In both displays, `[…]` omits damaged or unexpanded administrative fields.
The exact component witnesses below retain their labels and positions.

**Meaning:** Route messages through the Bavarian command in Munich, onward to the indicated formations or destinations. Do not use cable transmission; apply the specified army-key treatment and acknowledge receipt.

The place-name expansions, unit labels and administrative fields remain partly conjectural. `Doppelt` concerns the army-key instruction discussed in the historical report below.

| Source layer | Slots | Optimal split | Edit cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Typed text | 232 | 130 | 19 |
| Typed text plus handwritten groups | 242 | 130 | 24 |

The 242-slot alignment has 222 exact known-symbol matches. Exhaustive comparison gives a unique split at 130 in the prefix/suffix model, across all eight combinations of source layers and ambiguous glyphs. Treating both glyphs as unknown retains that split, at costs 17 and 22 for the typed and augmented layers. The resulting correspondence identifies the components; the cause of their combination remains unknown.

<a id="edition-cases-p158-component-readings"></a>

### Component readings

The p159 B frame has a duplicated five-coordinate group, a missing group, two erased coordinates and a source disagreement. In p159 C, comparison with the repeat reduces a six-coordinate group to five. Three edited component versions re-encrypt exactly using the established square cells, with the digit pair 5/6 unresolved. The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p158.json) records the repairs and raw readings.

<a id="edition-cases-p158-earlier-historical-reading-of-a-component"></a>

### Earlier historical reading of a component

Childs's report dated **20 November 1918**, printed on p42 of *German Military Ciphers from February to November 1918* (1935), deciphers order **11338**. Its SY→RVV via N4 header, 9 November date and 21:03 time agree with the p168 retransmission. [Primary report, p42](https://www.nsa.gov/Portals/75/documents/news-features/declassified-documents/friedman-documents/publications/FOLDER_268/41784789082381.pdf).

The report expands the garbled destination as `LANDWEHR REGIMENT; AN FECH`. The coordinate-derived `LA3DSBERGXAN0LECH` more closely suggests Landsberg an/am Lech; the exact expansion remains editorial. The surrounding report describes a separate **double-transposition army cipher**. It does not establish two complete ADFGVX encipherments.

The component bodies on **p168 C and D** are also discussed by **George Lasry,
Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** in §6.4 of
[*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461),
printed p23 / author-PDF p24. That credit also applies to the parallel p159 B/C bodies. Their gloss describes doubled confirmation; the raw text distinguishes the doubled army-key instruction from receipt acknowledgment.

The p158 composite identification and repair audit are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026**. The [historical comparison](../../data/reviews/historical_component_prior.json) records the earlier readings.

The [full p168 C witness](#edition-cases-radio-p168-munich-routing-witness) resolves the six-coordinate/four-coordinate group alignment. Its conditional frame fixes 139/140 raw positions, and an observed `V` from p159 B supplies the last coordinate. Twelve ownership aliases yield the same completed stream. The observed p168 pair `VG = K` also supports `GEN KDO`: adopting its G at p159 source 169 costs one `X→G` substitution, changing the H in `GEN HDO` above.

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses"></a>

## November 9: Danube report and Arad provisions

**Sources on this page:** p168 E. [Concise case study](../military/danube_arad_witnesses.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p164 C1](164.md#source-p164-c1).

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-november-9-danube-report-and-arad-provisions"></a>



These reports received on 9 November concern a Danube crossing and provisions at Arad for **80,000 men and 30,000 animals**. Source comparison restores a misread Danube-report glyph and eleven coordinates missing from the earlier Arad copy. The readings use the published **Nov7–9** key.

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-p164-c1"></a>

### p164 C1

**Readable German — conditional date and army completion:**

> AOK11. Abendmeldung 8.11.18. Lage der 11 Armee am 7.11 abends. Donauuebergang 219 I D beendet. Belgrad SEMUM. Lebhafter Uebersetzverkehr.

This first part of a five-part report describes the Eleventh Army's evening situation on 7 November: the 219th Infantry Division has completed its Danube crossing, with busy crossing traffic at `BELGRAD` and `SEMUM`. The proposed report date is 8 November 1918; interception followed early on 9 November. `SEMUM` retains the transmitted spelling.

The completion reads `8XC1X1?` as a day.month.year date and identifies `?1 ARMEE` with the `AOK11` already named at the start. The nearby [p155 report](../military/nov7_derailment_and_trains.md#p155-d) uses the fully observed date form `7X11X18`. These two contextual assumptions complete **124/124 positions** at a total cost of **five observed substitutions and five source-mask fills**.

| Field | Additional source changes, zero-based | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `8XC1X1?` → `8X11X18` | 139 `D` → `G`; 164 dash → `A` | Day.month.year interpretation within the 1918 sequence |
| `?1 ARMEE` → `11 ARMEE` | 52 invalid `C` → `G` | The same message opens with native `AOK11` |

Literal header: `C) ZON v UKS (1.57 a.m., November 9th); 2101 5 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-248`. [Source crop](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/sources/p164_C1.png).

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

The [shared Nov7–9 reference interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md) supplies **6** in the Arad footer, giving **RM 1C 186 GEH** and **136/136 conditional edited labels** in p168 E. The opposite assignment gives 185 GEH. Both coordinates of this VF pair are original observations. The four word substitutions, two printed-mask fills and one supplied gap coordinate remain unchanged.

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-p168-e"></a>

### p168 E

**Readable German — complete edited stream, preserving the unresolved fields and literal labels:**

> An OHL. Verpflegung noch 14 Tage. 10 Tage. Verpfleg. Zuege nach Arad. Arad bei ungar. Regierung erwirken. STAEKE 80000 Mann, 30000 Tiere. AOK11. RM 1C18?GEH.

The report requests provision trains to Arad and action through the Hungarian government. Both strength figures come directly from observed ciphertext pairs. The relationship between “14 Tage” and “10 Tage” remains unclear; the transmitted `STAEKE`, repeated Arad and closing labels are retained.

Literal header: `E) UKS v ZON (11.05 p.m., November 9th);AN LP 2000 KR; RICHI-272`. [Source crop](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/sources/p168_E.png).

The source prints 271 slots. In the conditional 272-slot frame, the short
group DDGX lacks one G present in p159’s DDGGX. Either insertion boundary
52 or 53 gives the same completed group. p159 also supplies the two printed
masks in VF--F. These three borrowed values change no observed p168 coordinate
and raise the reading from 132 to 135 fixed positions out of 136.

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-arad-cross-copy-restoration"></a>

### Arad cross-copy restoration

The p168 witness raises the earlier p159 primary frame from **124 to 135 fixed positions**. Its eleven supplied coordinates are all directly observed in p168, independent of the three values p168 borrows in the reverse comparison. This establishes the formerly uncertain strength field from surviving source pairs.

<details>
<summary>Restored p159 stream and complete source-family comparison</summary>

**Raw output — p159 primary geometry with all 11 missing coordinates supplied from observed p168 pairs:**

```text
0NOHLXVERPOLEGUNGNOCH14TAGEX10TAGEXXVERPFLEGXEUEGENACHARADXARADNEIUNGARXREGIERUNGERWIRKENXSTAEKE80000MANNX30000TISREXAOK11XRMX1CX18?GLHX
```

The coordinate-only comparison covers 173,580 canonical layouts and 694,320
source-origin maps. Five disagreements across 258 jointly observed positions
are the minimum. Only two canonical layouts remain: short-slot boundary 118
with five-slot boundaries (15,110) or (16,110). The four choices of duplicated
group origin give eight minimizing maps, all with one completed ciphertext
and 135/136 fixed labels. Each supplies its eleven additions from native
p168 observations.

Within this error family, coordinate comparison reduces the earlier 64 word-conditioned minima to eight and excludes all 48 P0000 alternatives. The earlier six-change objective fitted a word template; the present five-disagreement objective compares the received coordinates.

</details>

The common edited reading costs **seven observed substitutions in p159**
and **four in p168**. The extra p159 repair beyond its earlier six-word layer
adopts p168’s GEH footer spelling. Both copies keep the globally coupled
unknown digit. The [current p159 case](../military/arad_provisions_partial.md) now presents
this improved collation first, with the superseded U and P0000 hypotheses
in a historical comparison drawer.

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-source-and-prior-work"></a>

### Source and prior work

Childs printed pp164 and 168 correspond to PDF pp167 and 171. The separate
p159 Arad and p153 Danube sources provide the observed comparison material.
The Nov7–9 key remains credited to George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker (2016), and Lasry’s 2017 key list. Earlier contextual outputs and
p159/p153 work are retained in the [prior snapshot](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/prior_snapshot.json).
Source inspection, repeated-copy restoration and edition are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. The [source package](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/README.md) and [certificate](../../experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/certificates.json) record the complete comparisons. [Childs scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-reproduce-1"></a>

<a id="edition-cases-military-danube-arad-witnesses-reproduce"></a>

### Reproduce

```sh
python experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/verify.py --verify
python experiments/danube_arad_witnesses/verify.py --verify --pdf /path/to/childs.pdf
```

The verifier checks the exact displayed streams, coordinate origins, repair
prices, both global footer assignments and re-encryption. The optional PDF
check reproduces all reviewed source pixels.
